_meta.purpose: Page grammar for a contentpage: one hero, a repeatable body of content modules, one closing CTA.

hero.note: Exactly one hero, directly after the Header. Centered for a top-level entry, left-aligned for a subpage.

body.note: One section per content group. Mix the module types — a page of identical sections is a mono-layout and fails the composition rules.

cta.note: Exactly one closing CTA card as the final section.

rules: One consistent centered Medium (1024) content width for every section.
Home Page Hero for a centered top-level entry, Subpage Hero for a left-aligned subordinate page.
Heterogeneous content needs different module types; do not repeat one section shape for everything.
Content rows alternate: text-left then image-left, so the rhythm reads deliberate rather than accidental.

ONE primary action per page, offered twice: the hero and the closing CTA carry the SAME Brand action with the SAME label — once at the entry, once at the exit. The rule counts distinct goals, not button instances, so this is compliant. Two DIFFERENT Brand actions on one page are not.
The secondary action must also match between hero and CTA, or be omitted in both. Two different secondaries turn one offer into two competing ones.
Everything else is Filled or a Link. Navigation is always a Link, never a button.
Zebra background levels are optional and chosen intentionally; do not alternate section backgrounds by default.
Every Image ships EMPTY on Fill with a registered ratio. Use imageHash only for an asset the user already placed in the Figma file; there is no src option.
